Subject: Re: Weekly MAP checkpoint — data & deployment decisions (Cirrus Health)

Thanks Vivek —

Confirming a few constraints from our side:
- Preferred deployment: VPC peering in us-east-1 (we are not ready for full on-prem; we may revisit later).
- Retention: 180 days for model inputs; 2 year archival for logs (compressed).
- PII: patient identifiers counted as high-sensitivity; anything that qualifies as PHI must be redacted or tokenized before sending to hosted endpoints. We are open to hashing embeddings server-side if that meets compliance.
- KMS: BYOK required; key material must be resident in our AWS account.
- Timeline: we want an initial POC (evaluation) completed by 2027-04-20 and commercial close by the end of May if MAP milestones are met.

I will share a sanitized sample payload and the legal data handling checklist by Monday. Tom will join Friday's checkpoint for the architecture discussion.

Best,
Maya Liao
Sr. IT Security Manager, Cirrus Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Maya Liao <maya.liao@cirrushealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cirrushealth.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Weekly MAP checkpoint — decisions & action items (notes)

Vivek / team —

Notes and decisions from today's checkpoint (summary for the MAP):

Decisions (agreed):
- Deployment mode: Customer-managed VPC peering in us-east-1 (Dedicated capacity via Redwood Dedicated). On-prem not required for initial POC.
- Retention: 180 days for model inputs; application logs archived for 24 months in compressed buckets.
- PII handling: Token-level retention turned OFF for customer namespace; sensitive fields (PHI) will be redacted client-side when possible. For embeddings, we will use server-side hashing with salt in customer-owned KMS for any stored vector indexes.
- KMS: BYOK required; keys will remain in Cirrus Health AWS account with key policies granting Redwood service principal wrap/unwrap for inference operations.
- Evaluation & close timeline: POC complete target 2027-04-20; commercial close targeted by 2027-05-31 contingent on successful eval and SOC2 artifact review.

Action items (owner — due):
- Karthik Iyer — Draft security architecture diagram (network flow, peering, key wrap) and KMS integration notes. Due: 2027-04-07.
- Vivek Kulkarni — Update MAP worksheet with agreed milestones & close plan; coordinate cost estimate for Dedicated capacity. Due: 2027-04-09.
- Neha Kapoor — Compile SOC2 artifacts, consent logs, and audit table for Cirrus review; prepare a short evidence package. Due: 2027-04-08.
- Monica Patel — Schedule technical demo + ops walk-through for 2027-04-12; capture recording & transcript. Done: meeting invite sent.
- Maya Liao (Cirrus) — Share sanitized sample dataset and legal checklist. Due: 2027-04-06.

Meeting artifacts attached: MAP-action-item-log.docx, Zoom-Meeting-20270402.txt (meeting transcript excerpt).

Notes & rationale:
- We proposed an approach that minimizes egress and ensures key control for Cirrus while allowing Redwood to operate dedicated pools for predictable latency.
- Hashing embeddings with salted KMS wrap keeps vector search functionality while reducing PII exposure in persistent indexes.
- Retention windows selected to balance evaluation needs and auditability; archival bucket lifecycle policies to be included in the MAP worksheet.

Pending open questions:
- Does Cirrus require a formal Data Processing Addendum (DPA) clause tweak for KMS BYOK operations? Legal to confirm.
- If latency-sensitive endpoints need <100ms SLO, we may need a regional Dedicated burst; estimate required by Vivek (action).

Please review and flag any corrections. I'll upload the updated MAP worksheet after Vivek's cost inputs.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

--
